payload.headline: Micron jumps 19.04% to 707.7, reclaiming support; call moves from wait to hold

summary.thesis: Micron is an A-grade business earning record margins, and at 707.7 the price assumes free cash flow stops growing, but the trend is still down and those margins sit at a 5-year peak.
summary.decision: Long-term hold, since the price closed back above the level the last note set for returning to hold; no swing trade with resistance just overhead and earnings on 2026-12-17.
summary.act_at: Hold above 642.7; buy at 471.0; trim above 833.11

payload.happening: MU rose 19.04% in one day to 707.7. That takes it back above the 642.7–659.31 zone it broke on 2026-11-20. Our data has no news since the last note, so nothing here explains the jump. The next earnings report is due on 2026-12-17.
payload.business: Nothing in today's data changes the business itself. The last filing (quarter ended 2026-09-03) showed sales of 133.2B over the past year, up from 37.4B. The operating margin, meaning the share of sales left after running costs, was 74.59%, up from 26.14%. Free cash flow, meaning the cash left after spending on the business, was 59.0B, up from 1.7B. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 40.6B, with 38.4B of cash against 2.8B of debt. Margins are the real risk. The filings note that a 75% operating margin is at the top of a 5-year range that runs from -41% to 75%. Memory chip prices tend to move in cycles (general knowledge). Today's 19.04% move is a change in sentiment, not a change in the business. The operating margin the 2026-12-17 report shows will matter more than the price move.

worth.text: A standard cash-flow model can't be trusted here. Free cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year, and a jump like that can't be projected forward. Simpler checks help. At 707.7 the price works out to about 9.5 times past-year earnings and 6.0 times sales. The peer median is 7.2 times sales, so MU is cheap next to similar companies and fair against its own history (60th percentile of its 5-year range). The data says the current price implies free cash flow growth of -0.1%, meaning the market expects the 59.0B to stay flat. If cash flow just holds steady, it is worth 709.45 per share, almost exactly today's price. If it grows 10% at the start, the value is 1049.01. Against its own sales history, the middle value is 490.66. The gap between these methods comes down to one question: is today's margin permanent or a cyclical peak? If the operating margin falls to 37%, the value is 786.52, but that figure assumes 20% starting growth. That makes it the optimistic case, not the floor. My range runs from 490.66 (the history-based middle) to 709.45 (cash flow holds flat).
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near 59.0B instead of shrinking as the 74.59% operating margin fades from the top of its 5-year range.

bull: The price implies free cash flow growth of -0.1%. Any growth from 59.0B makes the stock worth more, with 1049.01 at 10% starting growth.
MU trades at 6.0 times sales against a peer median of 7.2, and at 9.5 times past-year earnings, despite 249.6% sales growth over the past year.
It is a grade A business (quality score 88) with 40.6B of net cash, so it can ride out a downturn.
bear: The 74.59% operating margin is up from 26.14% and sits at the top of a 5-year range that reaches as low as -41%. The filings say peaks like this usually fade.
The trend is down. The price is below its 20-day (776.85), 50-day (907.87) and 200-day (773.93) averages, and the 50-day is falling.

Options traders are cautious. There are 2.37 open puts (bets on a fall) for every open call, and the 2026-12-18 expiry priced a 21.4% move around earnings. That figure is from the 2026-11-20 chain, when the stock was at 594.51.

levels.what: Bottom of the 642.7–659.31 support zone the price just reclaimed. A close below it would move the call back to wait.
Top of the 435.76–471.0 zone, which has held 5 times. It is close to the 490.66 own-history middle value. This is the level to buy.
Top of the own-history price range (80th percentile price-to-sales). Above it, trim, because the price would assume the peak margin lasts.

longterm.why: The price closed above the 658.73 level the last note set as the trigger to return to hold. At 707.7 it sits at the top of the 490.66–709.45 range, so it is fair but leaves no margin of safety for new buying.

swing.why: Resistance at 729.46–746.07 is less than one ATR (average daily price range, 66.43) above the price, and the overall trend is still down. That leaves little upside for the risk. Wait for a pullback that holds the 642.7–659.31 zone, or a close above 746.07, before trading.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-17 report lands one day before the 2026-12-18 options expiry, which priced a 21.4% move, so any position opened before it carries that event risk. The operating margin it reports will decide whether the low or high end of the range applies.

change_mind: A close below 642.7 would move the call back to wait, because it would mean the support break of 2026-11-20 was real.
A close above 746.07, followed by a move through the 803.87–827.58 resistance zone, would show the downtrend has turned. Even then, trim above 833.11.
If the 2026-12-17 report shows sales falling quarter over quarter, against 30.81% growth last quarter, the margin peak would be fading, and 490.66 becomes the anchor value.
payload.what_changed: Changed: the call moves from wait to hold, because the 19.04% jump to 707.7 closed the price above 658.73, the level the last note named for returning to hold.
